analysis_name: WE format / span geometry — Validation v1.1
tokenization_rule: Unicode-aware lexical tokens: [letters/numbers] sequences are words; an internal apostrophe or hyphen remains inside the same token; punctuation-only tokens are excluded. Contractions, possessives, hyphenated forms, and numeric forms such as 1900's count as one token. The same rule is used for sentences, marked spans, corrections, and gaps.

span_type_definition.CLAUSE_OR_CLAUSE_LIKE: clause or clause-like unit identified with role/subtype/scope plus span length

correction_token_count_rule: max(source correction token count, target correction token count); no-correction claim=0; unparseable=null

measurement_confidence.span_position_and_gap: high when alignment_status=aligned; item status is preserved

items.sentence: The calibration of the instruments record stable readings during each trial.

marked_spans.label: A
marked_spans.text: The calibration of the instruments record

items.subtype: singular head noun in an of-phrase subject
items.answer_explanation: Calibration is the singular head of the subject noun phrase, so the main verb must be records.

items.sentence: The engineer selected several durability bearings for the test rig.
items.subtype: adjective required before a plural head noun
items.answer_explanation: The noun bearings needs an adjective modifier, so durable, not the noun durability, is required.

items.sentence: After the lighthouse crew had repaired the lamp, the keeper records the inspection details.

marked_spans.label: A
marked_spans.text: After the lighthouse crew had repaired the lamp,

items.subtype: simple past main verb after a past perfect subordinate clause
items.answer_explanation: The past perfect clause establishes a past time frame, so the main verb should be simple past recorded.

items.sentence: The archivist was deeply interested on maps from the coastal archive.

marked_spans.label: D
marked_spans.text: on maps from the coastal archive.

items.subtype: adjective-governed preposition in an interested-in phrase
items.answer_explanation: The established adjective-preposition collocation is interested in, not interested on.

items.sentence: The workshop focuses on carve wood and shaping clay for architectural models.
items.subtype: gerund complements coordinated after a training preposition
items.answer_explanation: The preposition on takes gerund complements, and carving must be parallel with shaping.

items.sentence: The engineer is responsible to the mountain station's ventilation system.
items.subtype: adjective complement after responsible for
items.answer_explanation: When responsible means having duty for something, it is followed by the preposition for.

items.sentence: The surveyor which mapped the village explained the boundary changes.
items.subtype: subject relative pronoun for a human antecedent
items.answer_explanation: The antecedent surveyor is a person and is the subject of mapped, so the relative marker should be who.

items.sentence: The museum restored a bronze finely decorated vessel from the collection.
items.subtype: participial adjective before a material adjective in a noun phrase
items.minimal_correction: bronze finely decorated vessel → finely decorated bronze vessel
items.answer_explanation: The participial modifier finely decorated precedes the material adjective bronze in the noun phrase.

items.sentence: The collection of oral histories contain vivid accounts of migration from the valley.

marked_spans.label: A
marked_spans.text: The collection of oral histories contain

items.subtype: singular head noun with an of-phrase interrupter
items.answer_explanation: The singular head noun collection controls agreement; the plural noun histories is inside an of-phrase.

items.sentence: Although the route was steep, but the hikers reached the summit before noon.
items.subtype: removal of a redundant coordinator after an although clause
items.answer_explanation: Although already introduces the subordinate contrast clause, so the additional coordinator but is unnecessary.

items.sentence: The manuscript was carefully restored the librarian last year.
items.subtype: passive transitive verb requiring a by-agent phrase
items.minimal_correction: restored the librarian → restored by the librarian
items.answer_explanation: In the passive construction, the agent must be introduced by by: restored by the librarian.

items.sentence: The team has carefully prepared the samples that they have record.
items.subtype: past participle after a perfect auxiliary
items.answer_explanation: The auxiliary have requires the past participle recorded.

items.sentence: It was placed beside the research equipment after the technician finished.
items.subtype: pronoun without an explicit antecedent
items.answer_explanation: The sentence supplies no antecedent for It; an explicit noun such as The sensor is needed.

items.sentence: The lecturer presented a scientifically overview of public water systems.
items.subtype: adjective required as a noun modifier after an article
items.answer_explanation: The noun overview requires the adjective scientific as its modifier, not the adverb scientifically.

items.sentence: The northern route is considerably more shorter than the southern route during winter.

marked_spans.label: C
marked_spans.text: more shorter than the southern route

items.subtype: comparative adjective without a redundant more marker
items.answer_explanation: Shorter is already a comparative form, so the redundant more must be removed.

items.sentence: The plants grew slowly during the trial because of the soil remained unusually cold.

marked_spans.label: D
marked_spans.text: of the soil remained unusually cold.

items.subtype: because clause rather than because-of before a finite clause
items.minimal_correction: because of the soil remained unusually cold → because the soil remained unusually cold
items.answer_explanation: A finite clause follows because, whereas because of must be followed by a noun phrase.

items.sentence: There is several balconies along the theater's upper gallery.
items.subtype: there-be agreement with a plural postposed noun phrase
items.answer_explanation: The plural postposed noun balconies requires the plural form are in the existential construction.

items.sentence: The analyst could not determine why did the values change after calibration.
items.subtype: embedded why-question with statement word order
items.minimal_correction: why did the values change → why the values changed
items.answer_explanation: The clause after determine is an embedded question and therefore uses statement order.

items.sentence: The strength of the coating is dependent of temperature and humidity.
items.subtype: adjective-governed dependent-on preposition
items.answer_explanation: The established collocation is dependent on, so of is the wrong preposition.

items.sentence: The committee recommends mapping the district and to revise its zoning plan.
items.subtype: gerund coordination after recommends
items.answer_explanation: The complements coordinated after recommends should be parallel gerund phrases: mapping and revising.

items.sentence: The seedlings grew rapid under the controlled lamps.
items.subtype: adverb required to modify a verb
items.answer_explanation: The verb grew requires the adverb rapidly to describe how the seedlings grew.

items.sentence: The panels, having built from recycled glass, were tested for strength.
items.subtype: reduced passive modifier before a finite passive predicate
items.minimal_correction: having built from recycled glass → built from recycled glass
items.answer_explanation: The panels receive the action, so the reduced modifier must be passive: built from recycled glass.

items.sentence: After the bridge had been inspected, engineers approves the repair plan.

marked_spans.label: A
marked_spans.text: After the bridge had been inspected,

items.subtype: simple past main verb after a past perfect passive clause
items.answer_explanation: The completed inspection places the following event in the past, so the main verb should be approved.

items.sentence: The questionnaire included much responses from first-year students.
items.subtype: countable quantifier before a plural count noun
items.answer_explanation: Responses is a plural count noun, so it requires the quantifier many rather than much.

items.sentence: The seedlings grew surprising quickly in the greenhouse.
items.subtype: adverb required to modify an adverb
items.answer_explanation: The word modifies the adverb quickly, so it must be the adverb surprisingly.

items.sentence: An ecosystem supports many forms of life.
items.subtype: article before a singular count noun
items.answer_explanation: The article an correctly precedes the singular count noun ecosystem.

items.sentence: The railway opened the mountain route in 1898.
items.subtype: simple past in a dated historical sequence
items.answer_explanation: The dated event correctly uses the simple past.

items.sentence: The study reports significant changes in memory.
items.subtype: adjective modifying a research noun
items.answer_explanation: The adjective significant correctly modifies the noun changes.

items.sentence: Several methods improve the harvest yield.
items.subtype: quantifier with a plural count noun
items.minimal_correction: D: the harvest yield → the harvest yields
items.answer_explanation: The planned correction makes the quantified count noun plural.

items.sentence: The course emphasizes reading critically and writing clearly.
items.subtype: parallel gerund phrases after a coordinator
items.answer_explanation: The two gerund phrases are parallel after emphasizes.

items.sentence: The plateau appears stable during the dry season.
items.subtype: adjective complement after a linking verb
items.answer_explanation: Appears correctly takes the predicate adjective stable.

items.sentence: Scientists are committed to protecting the coral reef.
items.subtype: gerund as the object of a preposition
items.answer_explanation: The preposition to is correctly followed by the gerund protecting.

items.sentence: The arch that supports the roof was recently repaired.
items.subtype: relative pronoun as the subject of a restrictive clause
items.minimal_correction: D: was recently repaired → was recently repaired
items.answer_explanation: That correctly serves as the subject of the restrictive relative clause.

items.sentence: The rapidly moving clouds covered the horizon.
items.subtype: adverb modifying a participle
items.answer_explanation: Rapidly is the adverb modifying moving.

items.sentence: Investors are concerned about the sudden change.
items.subtype: preposition selected for a noun phrase
items.answer_explanation: Concerned correctly combines with the preposition about.

items.sentence: Each participant submitted their questionnaire before leaving.
items.subtype: pronoun agreement with a singular antecedent
items.minimal_correction: C: their questionnaire → his or her questionnaire
items.answer_explanation: The singular antecedent each participant requires a singular pronoun in the locked construction.

items.sentence: The survey measured both public trust and policy awareness.
items.subtype: parallel noun phrases after both and
items.minimal_correction: D: and policy awareness → and policy awareness
items.answer_explanation: Both coordinates the parallel noun phrases public trust and policy awareness.

items.sentence: The vaccine was tested on volunteers before approval.
items.subtype: passive voice with an object receiving an action
items.answer_explanation: The vaccine correctly receives the action in the passive construction.

items.sentence: The poems written during exile reveal a new style.
items.subtype: adjective phrase in postmodifier position
items.minimal_correction: B: written during exile → written during exile
items.answer_explanation: The participial adjective phrase correctly follows and modifies poems.

items.sentence: Using infrared sensors, the robot avoids obstacles.
items.subtype: present participle in a reduced active clause
items.answer_explanation: Using correctly introduces a reduced active clause whose understood subject is the robot.

items.sentence: The court published its decision on Monday.
items.subtype: definite article for a uniquely identified institution
items.minimal_correction: D: on Monday → on the Monday
items.answer_explanation: The planned correction supplies the definite article in the marked institutional time phrase.

items.sentence: The second estimate is more precise than the first.
items.subtype: comparative adjective with than
items.minimal_correction: A: The second estimate → The second estimate
items.answer_explanation: More precise correctly forms the comparative with than.

items.sentence: The device allows operators to adjust the pressure.
items.subtype: verb governed by an infinitive complement
items.answer_explanation: Allow correctly takes an object followed by an infinitive complement.

items.sentence: The conductor raised the baton and began the performance.
items.subtype: parallel finite verbs coordinated by and
items.minimal_correction: C: raised the baton and began → raised the baton and began
items.answer_explanation: Raised and began are parallel finite verbs coordinated by and.

items.sentence: The artifact provides evidence of early settlement.
items.subtype: noun required as the object of a preposition
items.answer_explanation: Settlement is the noun required after the preposition of.

items.sentence: The star whose spectrum changed was observed again.
items.subtype: whose for a possessive relative relationship
items.answer_explanation: Whose correctly marks the possessive relationship between star and spectrum.

items.sentence: Although costs increased, the program continued to expand.
items.subtype: although introducing a finite concessive clause
items.answer_explanation: Although correctly introduces the finite concessive clause.

items.sentence: The patient had recovered before the physician arrived.
items.subtype: past perfect before a later past event
items.answer_explanation: Had recovered correctly marks the earlier of the two past events.

items.sentence: Few residents opposed the construction plan.
items.subtype: few with a plural count noun
items.minimal_correction: D: the construction plan → the construction plans
items.answer_explanation: The planned correction makes the quantified count noun plural.

items.sentence: To reduce emissions, the city expanded its solar program.
items.subtype: infinitive of purpose before a main clause
items.minimal_correction: A: To reduce emissions → To reduce emissions
items.answer_explanation: The infinitive phrase correctly expresses the purpose of the main clause.

items.sentence: A architect measured the vaulted entrance before the renovation began.
items.subtype: indefinite article before a consonant-initial noun
items.answer_explanation: The consonant letter a is pronounced with an initial vowel sound, so the article must be an.

items.sentence: The region experienced a dramatically temperature shift during the afternoon.
items.subtype: adjective required before a head noun
items.answer_explanation: Dramatic is the adjective required to modify temperature; dramatically is an adverb.

items.sentence: The clinic introduced the screening program after it identify the main risk factors.
items.subtype: simple past finite verb in a completed historical sequence
items.answer_explanation: The completed past event requires the simple past identified.

items.sentence: The course emphasizes reading technical articles, analyzing evidence, and to present findings clearly.
items.subtype: parallel gerund complements in a coordinated list
items.answer_explanation: The three complements after emphasizes must use parallel gerund forms.

items.sentence: The court found the new evidence convincing for the jury.
items.subtype: adjective object complement after find
items.answer_explanation: In this frame, the adjective convincing takes to before the recipient of the persuasion.

items.sentence: The buses traveling along the old route, carrying commuters into the city each morning.
items.subtype: present participle in a reduced active clause
items.minimal_correction: The buses travel along the old route, carrying commuters into the city each morning.
items.answer_explanation: The sentence needs a finite main verb; traveling alone leaves the subject without a predicate.

items.sentence: Despite the market was unstable, investors continued to purchase municipal bonds.
items.subtype: although introducing a finite concessive clause
items.answer_explanation: A finite clause requires although, whereas despite must be followed by a noun phrase or gerund.

items.sentence: The plant is one of the species with whom the botanist has worked for years.

marked_spans.label: D
marked_spans.text: the botanist has worked for years

items.subtype: relative pronoun as the object of a preposition
items.answer_explanation: Which refers to the plant species; whom is used for people.

items.sentence: The pattern of clouds over the mountain indicate an approaching storm.
items.subtype: subject-verb agreement across an intervening modifier
items.answer_explanation: The singular head noun pattern requires indicates.

items.sentence: Only much of the dietary samples contained enough iron for the analysis.
items.subtype: quantifier compatible with a countable plural noun
items.answer_explanation: Samples is a countable plural noun, so many, not much, is required.

items.sentence: The lecturer discussed the historical develop of the regional dialect.
items.subtype: noun required as the head of a prepositional object
items.answer_explanation: The premodifier historical requires the noun development as the head of the phrase.

items.sentence: The components were assembling in a sealed chamber to prevent contamination.
items.subtype: passive participle after a finite form of be
items.answer_explanation: The components receive the action, so be must be followed by the passive participle assembled.

items.sentence: The proposal addresses not only traffic congestion but also should improve pedestrian safety.
items.subtype: parallel noun phrases after not only but also
items.answer_explanation: The two objects of addresses must be parallel noun phrases: traffic congestion and pedestrian safety.

items.sentence: The analyst succeeded in predict the quarterly trend despite limited data.
items.subtype: gerund as the complement of a preposition
items.answer_explanation: The preposition in takes a gerund complement, predicting.

items.sentence: The eastern plateau is high than the valley during the dry season.
items.subtype: comparative adjective required by than
items.answer_explanation: Than requires the comparative form higher.

items.sentence: The museum displayed a clay ancient vessel from the excavation.
items.subtype: adjective order inside a noun phrase
items.minimal_correction: an ancient clay vessel from the excavation
items.answer_explanation: The age adjective precedes the material adjective: an ancient clay vessel.

items.sentence: Each storyteller adapted their account to suit the audience.
items.subtype: singular pronoun agreement with an indefinite antecedent
items.answer_explanation: In the locked traditional agreement pattern, singular each requires a singular pronoun.

items.sentence: The amendment appears in constitutional after the court's review.
items.subtype: predicate adjective after a linking verb
items.answer_explanation: Appear takes the predicate adjective directly; the inserted preposition in is not part of the linking-verb frame.

items.sentence: The librarian organized the archived manuscripts methodical.
items.subtype: adverb required to modify a research verb
items.answer_explanation: The verb organized is modified by the adverb methodically, not the adjective methodical.

items.sentence: The volunteers collected water samples monitor pollution levels in the wetland.
items.subtype: infinitive of purpose after a finite verb
items.answer_explanation: The infinitive marker to is required before the purpose verb monitor.

items.sentence: The observatory benefits from clear skies and benefits to precise measurements.
items.subtype: fixed preposition collocation after benefit
items.answer_explanation: Benefit takes the preposition from when it means to gain an advantage from something.

items.sentence: The conductor rehearsed the ensemble and checking the balance of the brass section.

marked_spans.label: D
marked_spans.text: the balance of the brass section

items.subtype: parallel finite verbs in a coordinated predicate
items.answer_explanation: Rehearsed and checked are coordinated finite past-tense verbs with the same subject.

items.sentence: Each of the historic vehicles require careful maintenance.
items.subtype: singular agreement after each
items.answer_explanation: The subject each is singular, so the verb must be requires.

items.sentence: The geologists realized that the glacier melted before they had reached the valley.
items.subtype: past perfect for the earlier of two past events
items.answer_explanation: The earlier melting event takes the past perfect had melted relative to the later realization.

items.sentence: The treatment plant needs something useful for removing sediment efficiently.
items.subtype: postpositive adjective phrase following an indefinite pronoun
items.minimal_correction: needs something to remove sediment efficiently
items.answer_explanation: The adjective useful does not express the intended function; the unique grammatical repair is the purpose infinitive to remove.
